newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics sees FY97 revs near $3 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics sees FY97 revs near $3 bln.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp said on Monday it expects overall revenues in fiscal year 1997 to be in line with analysts' estimates of just below $3 billion.
The company reported fiscal 1996 revenues of $1.98 billion earlier Monday.

"With respect to overall growth for next year, we would expect total revenues for 1997 to fall within a range essentially consistent with estimates," said chief financial officer Mark Remissong, adding that consensus analysts' estimates called for revenues "slightly below $3 billion."

U.S. Robotics also sought to allay fears about when its X2 modem with downloading capabilities of 56 kilobit per second would be available. Company officers said the model would be ready by the early 1997, as it initially projected.

"We are on that schedule and intend to remain on it, and we don't expect to have any difficulties meeting those objectives," John McCartney, chief operating officer, said in a conference call with reporters.

McCartney also said initial tests have shown the X2 technology works on about 95 percent of incoming calls to Internet service providers. He cited an industry report that said some 85 percent of users in the United States will be able to use the 56 kpps modem.
Recently the ability of a 56 kbps connection over regular telephone lines has been called into question.
"This seems to be an issue that has come up recently and just is not based at all on evidence we've generated," McCartney said.
